title: Tenant upgrade notice templates, SLO/SLA appendix, and Terraform guidance

sla_summary: Availability SLA: 99.9% monthly for core inference API endpoints (excluding agreed maintenance windows). Response SLA: Severity 1 response within 1 hour, Severity 2 within 4 hours. Credits: standard percentage credit tiers tied to monthly uptime SLA breaches per contract. Maintenance windows that are pre-approved and communicated with required notice are excluded from uptime calculations.
escalation_contacts: Evelyn Marques — Private Deployments Lead — evelyn@redwood.example.com
maintenance_impact_levels: Impact: None — informational only (no customer-visible interruption).
Impact: Degraded — reduced throughput or longer tail latency; retries recommended.
Impact: Brief outage — short window (<= 5 minutes) of unavailability to a single tenant during rolling restart.
Impact: Maintenance outage — planned downtime longer than 5 minutes, scheduled and pre-approved; may require application-level retries.
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working playbook contains templates and guidance for customer communications, SLO/SLA clarifications, and Terraform upgrade notes for private deployments (VPC or on-prem). It is intended for use by Solutions Engineering, SRE, and Customer Success during planned tenant upgrades or platform maintenance that affects private customers.

Summary guidance (short):
- Determine impact level (see Impact Levels).
- Confirm maintenance window with customer and internal teams.
- Send staged communications: 14-day notice (when applicable), 72-hour, 24-hour, 1-hour, and post-maintenance summary.
- Update ticketing and status pages; if persistent issues occur escalate per escalation_contacts.

SLO vs SLA: short primer
- SLO: operational targets we measure (e.g., 99.95% p95 latency under normal load, 99.9% availability excluding maintenance). SLOs drive alerts and ops playbooks.
- SLA: contractual guarantee with credits/penalties. Maintenance windows that meet the notice & duration rules in the contract are excluded from SLA uptime calculation. Always confirm the exact contract clauses when planning work that could touch SLA boundaries.

Pre-notice checklist (internal):
- Confirm TF plan and backup snapshot complete and stored.
- Validate rollback plan and smoke tests.
- Confirm cust contact and maintenance approval window.
- Notify internal teams: SRE, Security, Customer Success, Sales Engineering.
- Prepare monitoring dashboards and synthetic tests for pre/post verification.

Communication templates (placeholders in {{}}):
1) 14-day advisory (use if upgrade requires advanced scheduling)
Subject: [Advisory] Planned maintenance window for your deployment — {{start_date}}
Body: Hello {{customer_name}} team,

We are scheduling a planned upgrade to your private deployment ({{deployment_id}}) on {{start_date}} between {{start_time}} and {{end_time}} ({{timezone}}). This upgrade includes kernel-level security patches, an inference runtime update, and Terraform-managed networking adjustments. Expected impact: {{impact_level}}.

What to expect:
- Estimated interruption: {{estimated_downtime}} (if any)
- Actions required from you: {{customer_actions_or_none}}
- Rollback window: {{rollback_cutoff}}

If this window is inconvenient, please reply with alternative availability within 3 business days.

Best,
Redwood Private Deployments Team

2) 72-hour reminder
Subject: Reminder: upcoming maintenance for {{customer_name}} — {{start_date}}
Body: Hello,

This is a reminder that we will perform the scheduled maintenance on {{start_date}} from {{start_time}} to {{end_time}}. Contact for urgent questions: {{primary_contact_email}}.

Monitoring plan: We will run smoke tests before and after the window and keep status updated at the customer ticket.

3) 24-hour confirmation
Subject: Confirmed: Maintenance tomorrow for {{customer_name}}
Body: Hello {{customer_name}},

Confirming maintenance begins at {{start_time}} {{timezone}}. Please ensure any critical jobs are paused or can tolerate retries during this window. We will post a completion message and the results of our validation tests after the window closes.

4) 1-hour pre-start
Subject: Starting maintenance in 1 hour — {{customer_name}}
Body: Starting in 1 hour. Minimal impact expected ({{impact_level}}). If you observe severe issues, open a ticket at {{support_link}} or call {{sre_phone}}.

5) Post-maintenance summary
Subject: Maintenance completed — summary for {{customer_name}} ({{start_date}})
Body: Maintenance complete. Summary:
- Start: {{start_datetime}}
- End: {{end_datetime}}
- Validation: smoke tests passed (list), latency at p50/p95 numbers before/after: {{p50_before}}/{{p50_after}} / {{p95_before}}/{{p95_after}}
- Issues encountered: {{issues_or_none}}
- Follow-up actions: {{followups_or_none}}

If you have any questions or see residual issues, reply to this thread.

Operational runbook snippets (brief):
- Pre-checks: terraform plan approved, snapshots created, control-plane backups verified.
- Apply phase: drain service on node A, apply terraform changes, run schema/migration scripts if needed, restart processes, run smoke tests, uncordon node, move to node B and repeat.
- Rollback: if smoke tests fail, restore from snapshot if config rollback cannot be applied, notify customer and SRE oncall, trigger incident process.

Terraform guidance (high-level, copy-ready snippet below should be adapted):
- Always run terraform plan in a disposable workspace matching customer vars.
- Use lifecycle rules and replace triggers for sensitive resources.
- Keep module versions pinned in terraform.tfvars for reproducible upgrades.

Terraform snippet (example string to paste into terraform files; adapt vars):
module "redwood_private_network" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//private-network?ref=v1.3.2"
  customer_id = var.customer_id
  region = var.region
  vpc_cidr = var.vpc_cidr
  allowed_ips = var.customer_admin_ips
  tag = "customer-${var.customer_id}"
  lifecycle = {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

Terraform notes (short bullets):
- Note 1: Use provider aliasing when the upgrade requires interacting with both existing and freshly created cloud accounts.
- Note 2: For on-prem, ensure the tfstate is stored in an approved remote backend (S3/GCS with encryption) and that access is audited.
- Note 3: If changing network ACLs, coordinate with customer network Ops 7+ days in advance.

Post-upgrade verification checklist (internal):
- All smoke tests pass for inference, embeddings, and health endpoints.
- KV cache warms to baseline within {{warmup_window}}.
- No elevated error budget burn post-upgrade for 24 hours.
- Confirm logs and traces routed to customer-approved destinations.

Example escalation blurb (to include in ticket):
If critical failure after maintenance: This is an urgent escalation for tenant upgrade failure for {{customer_name}}. Steps attempted: terraform rollback attempted at {{time}}; snapshot restore initiated at {{time}}; SRE oncall paged at {{time}}. Current status: {{status}}.

Notes and caveats:
- Always cross-check the customer contract for maintenance notice requirements (some enterprise customers require 30+ days).
- For security patches that are emergency-critical we may trigger an exclusion path from standard notice but must still document post-facto and coordinate with legal.

Appendix: metrics to include in post-maintenance message
- Request rate (RPS) and 95/99 latency percentiles for core endpoints before and after.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) comparison.
- Token/sec throughput baseline and peak.
- Node-level CPU/GPU utilization samples.

End of document working-draft. Use this as the basis for customer-specific edits and legal review when a customer’s contract requires special handling.
terraform_notes: Keep module refs pinned: avoid implicit latest tags for infra modules.
Run terraform validate + plan in CI with customer varset before approving any apply.
Use lifecycle.prevent_destroy on customer-critical resources; add replace_triggers for optional replacements.
Example: set tf workspace to 'cust-{{customer_id}}-upgrade' and keep a persisted plan artifact for auditing.
Ensure tfstate backend encryption and limited access; rotate backend creds after major upgrades.
